featured_reviews.name: Dr Anuradha Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Film Studios: The Heart of Cinematic Magic

Film studios are the creative powerhouses that bring stories to life, turning scripts into immersive visual experiences. These spaces are more than just physical locations—they are hubs of imagination, where directors, actors, and technicians collaborate to craft films that captivate audiences worldwide. From grand soundstages to cutting-edge post-production facilities, film studios play a vital role in shaping the magic of cinema. Whether producing large-scale blockbusters or intimate indie films, these studios provide the foundation for storytelling at its finest, blending artistry with technical brilliance.

Yash Raj Films: A Legacy of Excellence in Indian Cinema

Yash Raj Films (YRF) stands as a pillar of Indian cinema, synonymous with grandeur, romance, and timeless storytelling. Founded by the visionary Yash Chopra, YRF has redefined Bollywood with its unparalleled craftsmanship, producing films that resonate across generations. From heartwarming love stories to gripping thrillers, the studio has consistently set new benchmarks in filmmaking. Beyond its artistic brilliance, YRF has also built an empire with its state-of-the-art studios, fostering talent and innovation. With its keen eye for storytelling and commitment to excellence, Yash Raj Films continues to shape the future of Indian cinema, leaving an indelible mark on audiences worldwide.

featured_reviews.name: Kevin Loilargosain
featured_reviews.review_text:
A fantastic and interactive Bollywood experience!

What a great experience! This tour is an absolute must if you're looking for an incredibly fun and interactive outing.

We started our day by dressing up in various iconic Bollywood outfits. We took pictures in these, which were then edited so professionally that it felt like we were in a real movie! After that, we hit the studio to sing our hearts out to famous Bollywood songs. As a great finale to this part, we even got to dance along with real Bollywood dancers.

Next, we were given a fascinating tour through the different studios. It was incredibly fun and special to get a peek at an active film set! After that, we were guided through the other studios and received engaging explanations about the whole process. This really brought the magic of filmmaking to life for us.

Finally, I want to give a huge compliment to the staff: everyone was incredibly friendly, enthusiastic, and helpful. They truly made this experience complete!

review_photos.caption: 🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Bollywood films often shoot in various locations, from the vibrant streets of Mumbai to scenic rural landscapes across India.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Behind-the-scenes, the set is a bustling environment filled with crew members, including cinematographers, sound technicians, and makeup artists.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Bollywood, the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai, is one of the largest and most prolific film industries in the world.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Many Bollywood films promote messages of love, family values, and social issues, resonating deeply with Indian audiences.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The popularity of Bollywood extends beyond India, with a large fan base in countries like the USA, UK, Canada, and several parts of Africa and the Middle East.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Bollywood films are known for their colorful song and dance sequences, often featuring elaborate choreography and vibrant costumes.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The production process can be complex, often requiring multiple takes to capture the perfect scene and ensuring high-quality results.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Editing is done after filming, where editors piece together footage to create a cohesive narrative and enhance the film’s pace.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Bollywood often celebrates cultural festivals and events, incorporating them into the storyline, showcasing the richness of Indian traditions.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - A typical Bollywood film can have a runtime of anywhere from 90 minutes to over three hours, with many incorporating an intermission.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The industry produces over 1,500 films annually, showcasing a wide range of genres, including romance, drama, action, and comedy.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Filmmakers often conduct extensive location scouting to find the perfect backdrop for key scenes, which adds authenticity to the film.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The director plays a pivotal role in guiding the artistic vision of the film, collaborating closely with actors and crew throughout the process.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The art department is responsible for sourcing props and decorations that align with the film’s theme, ensuring authenticity and creativity.

🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The term “Bollywood” is a portmanteau of “Bombay” (the former name of Mumbai) and “Hollywood,” reflecting its cinematic aspirations.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The music of Bollywood films is an essential element, often released as soundtracks before the film’s premiere and contributing to its marketing.

featured_reviews.name: Indiana Jonas
featured_reviews.review_text:
We joined this tour expecting a true immersion into the world of Bollywood.
The studio is indeed a real working studio used for filming, but the experience offered does not quite match what one might imagine from a “Bollywood tour.”

You get to see sets and filming areas, but it is not access to major film productions or the behind-the-scenes world of iconic Bollywood movies. The visit feels more like a tourist-oriented presentation than an authentic insight into the Indian film industry.

It is not a bad visit in itself, but it may create expectations that are not fully aligned with reality. In my view, it is not truly a Bollywood experience in the way it is advertised.

name: Chandivali Studio
description: Chandivali “Studio,” As It Is Known, Began Its Journey In 1940 When Chandrarao Kadam Purchased A Large Parcel Of Land At Chandivali, Near Powai Lake In Mumbai, India. His Idea Was To Create Multiple And Diverse Filming Locations In One Place, Use Them For Shooting His Own Films But Also Make These Locations Available To Other Film Producers. This Innovative Concept Was Unprecedented In The Indian Movie Industry And Became A Template That Many Others Would Follow. It Took Mr. Kadam Nearly Four Years To Clear And Level The Existing Forestland And A Lifetime To Create And Develop The Parcel’s Various Themed Areas. Chandivali Outdoor Location Opened For Business In 1944.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Bollywood Park is a decent place to visit, but not as grand as expected. Most of the film sets are either covered or not accessible, so you only get a glimpse of a few memorable spots like Taarak Mehta ka Ooltah Chasmah sets from far that are ok for quick photos.

The museum section is actually nice for clicking pictures, with well-designed setups and film-themed decor. The live show was the highlight well performed and quite engaging. Overall, it’s good for a one-time visit, especially if you enjoy Bollywood vibes, but don’t go in expecting full studio-style access as ticket price does not justify it.

featured_reviews.name: Mesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
HIGHLIGHT - If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

My recent visit to Mumbai Film City was far from what I had hoped. To start, the nearest metro station is Aarey, it is about 4 km away. From there, take an auto (no more than ₹150) straight to the official ticket counter. Be cautious, several individuals may try to sell you tickets along the way at inflated prices. Avoid them, as they are scammers.

After a long wait, we were taken inside the premises by an AC bus. Unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming from the beginning. Compared to Hyderabad's Film City, this one feels small, restricted, and poorly organized. Most of what you see are large tin sheets covering the sets, there is no access to the actual sets themselves. It felt like being shown billboards of what you could see, but never actually do.

The tour ends at Bollywood Park, which hosts a few staged performances. This was the only mildly enjoyable part. The on site restaurant is strictly vegetarian, which may not appeal to everyone, and the food was overpriced for its quality.

Overall, Mumbai Film City lacks substance, feels commercialized, and fails to deliver the behind the scenes magic one would expect. If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.
